answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by staking reputation on a trust ridge: each new agent begins at the nadir of credibility, holding no weight in consensus until it co-signs verifiable work with established peers. As it delivers, its score climbs the ridge, locked as collateral in a vault that slashing can drain if the agent ever colludes or double-votes. Creating a thousand fresh identities grants each nothing, because influence costs something to lose. Identity stays cheap while weight stays expensive, pushing attackers toward honest participation rather than duplication.
